:::{#exm-direct-proof}
#### The square of an odd integer is odd

Claim: if $n$ is an [odd](number-systems.qmd#def-odd) [integer](number-systems.qmd#def-integers),
then $n^2$ is odd.

Since $n$ is odd,
there is an integer $k$ with $n = 2k + 1$.
Then

$$
\ba
n^2
&= (2k + 1)^2
&& \text{(substitute } n = 2k + 1 \text{)}
\\&= (2k)^2 + 2 \cd 2k \cd 1 + 1^2
&& \text{(square of a sum)}
\\&= 4k^2 + 4k + 1
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\\&= 2(2k^2 + 2k) + 1
&& \text{(distributive law, read from right to left)}
\ea
$$

and $2k^2 + 2k$ is an integer,
because adding or multiplying [integers](number-systems.qmd#def-integers) gives an integer.
So $n^2 = 2 \cd (\text{an integer}) + 1$, which is the definition of odd.
For example,

$$
\begin{aligned}
n &= 7 \\
&= 2 \cd 3 + 1
\end{aligned}
$$

gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
n^2 &= 49 \\
&= 2 \cd 24 + 1,
\end{aligned}
$$

and $2 \cd 3^2 + 2 \cd 3 = 24$.

The proof above that
[the sum of two even integers is even](#exm-proof)
is also a [direct proof](#def-direct-proof).

:::
